stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Jan 2025 second term
frames.note: The story begins when Trump returns to office and starts describing Beijing as a co-equal great power rather than a rival to be contained. Under this opening, the current G7 friction, NATO spending demands and outreach to Pyongyang read as one continuous reset built around that reframe. This is the frame Trump-aligned outlets and the White House itself open with.

frames.label: 2018 tariff round
frames.note: The story begins with the Section 301 tariffs and the formal turn to strategic competition with China. Under this opening, today's peer-power language is the latest move inside an eight-year confrontation that the first Trump term started and Biden largely kept. This is the frame China hawks, US trade officials and most Taipei-based coverage open with.

frames.label: 1972 Nixon opening
frames.note: The story begins with Nixon's trip to Beijing and the long bet that engagement would shape Chinese behavior. Under this opening, the current reframing is one more swing in a fifty-year cycle of opening, integration and pullback between two powers that have always managed each other as peers in practice. This is the frame realist historians, Russian and Chinese state outlets and many European analysts open with.

bands.label: Second term reset
bands.summary: Trump returns to office and reworks the China file around direct leader-to-leader dealings, tariff bargaining and a softer public vocabulary toward Beijing, Moscow and Pyongyang.

nodes.title: Trump sworn in for second term
nodes.what: Donald Trump took the oath of office as the 47th president, returning to the White House four years after leaving it. His inaugural address emphasized restoring American strength through deal-making and signaled a shift from alliance-led containment toward direct leader-to-leader diplomacy with rival powers including China and Russia.

cites.l: Wikipedia: Second inauguration of Donald Trump

nodes.title: Executive order imposes 10 percent tariff on Chinese imports
nodes.what: Trump signed an executive order applying an additional 10 percent tariff on goods from China, citing the flow of fentanyl precursors as the legal trigger under emergency economic powers. Beijing responded within days with targeted duties on US energy and farm equipment and opened a WTO complaint, framing the move as an opening bid rather than a final break.

nodes.title: Reciprocal tariff package announced
nodes.what: Trump announced a sweeping reciprocal tariff schedule he called Liberation Day, raising the headline rate on Chinese goods sharply while applying lower baseline tariffs on most other trading partners. The package distinguished China from allies by margin rather than by category, which the White House described as recognition of Beijing's scale as a trading peer.
nodes.disputed: The administration described the move as forcing a fair bilateral reset between the world's two largest economies; Chinese state media described it as unilateral coercion dressed up as reciprocity.

nodes.title: Geneva talks produce 90-day tariff pause
nodes.what: After two days of meetings in Geneva, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng announced a 90-day suspension of most of the new reciprocal tariffs, rolling rates back toward pre-April levels while negotiations continued. The joint statement used the language of mutual respect and equal footing, a shift in register from the prior Biden-era export-control framing.

nodes.title: Trump and Xi meet on the margins of APEC
nodes.what: Trump and Xi Jinping met in person in South Korea around the APEC leaders' summit, their first face-to-face encounter of the second term. The readouts from both sides described soybean purchases, fentanyl cooperation and a further tariff pause, and Trump publicly referred to the United States and China as the world's two great powers that would have to manage the century together.
nodes.disputed: The White House readout described the meeting as Trump securing concrete Chinese concessions on trade and narcotics; the Chinese readout described it as Xi setting the terms for a stable peer-to-peer relationship.

bands.label: Strategic competition era
bands.summary: Section 301 tariffs, tech export controls, the Phase One deal and Biden-era chip restrictions lock in a bipartisan framing of China as the central long-term competitor.

nodes.title: Trump signs Section 301 memorandum on China
nodes.what: After a USTR investigation concluded that Chinese practices on technology transfer and intellectual property were unreasonable, President Trump signed a presidential memorandum directing tariffs and WTO action against China. The move marked the formal pivot from engagement to strategic competition as the organizing US trade posture toward Beijing.

nodes.title: First Section 301 tariffs take effect
nodes.what: The United States imposed 25 percent tariffs on roughly 34 billion dollars of Chinese imports, and Beijing matched them within hours on US goods. Successive tariff rounds followed through 2018 and 2019, restructuring large parts of bilateral trade and supply chains.

nodes.title: Huawei added to the Commerce Department Entity List
nodes.what: Citing national security concerns, the Commerce Department placed Huawei and dozens of affiliates on the Entity List, sharply restricting US technology exports to the company. The action extended the contest from tariffs into semiconductors, 5G equipment and the global tech stack.

nodes.title: Phase One trade agreement signed
nodes.what: Trump and Chinese Vice Premier Liu He signed a Phase One agreement in which China committed to higher purchases of US goods and to specific changes on intellectual property and financial services, while most existing US tariffs remained in place. The deal paused escalation without unwinding the new tariff baseline.
nodes.disputed: USTR describes Phase One as enforceable structural reform paired with large purchase commitments; later academic and Peterson Institute reviews describe it as a tariff truce whose purchase targets China never met.

nodes.title: Biden administration imposes sweeping chip export controls
nodes.what: The Commerce Department issued rules restricting exports to China of advanced semiconductors, chipmaking equipment and the services of US persons supporting Chinese chip fabs. The package generalized the Huawei-era approach into a sector-wide effort to slow Chinese progress in AI-grade computing.

nodes.title: US military shoots down Chinese high-altitude balloon
nodes.what: A US F-22 destroyed a Chinese balloon off the South Carolina coast after it crossed the continental United States, prompting Secretary of State Blinken to postpone a planned trip to Beijing. The episode briefly froze top-level diplomatic contact and hardened public framing of China as a security threat.
nodes.disputed: US officials described the balloon as a surveillance platform that violated sovereign airspace; Beijing described it as a civilian weather craft blown off course and called the shootdown an overreaction.

bands.label: WTO integration
bands.summary: China joins the WTO and is treated by successive US administrations as a rising stakeholder to be engaged, even as trade imbalances, South China Sea moves and Xi's consolidation steadily harden the mood in Washington.

nodes.title: China formally accedes to the World Trade Organization
nodes.what: After fifteen years of negotiations, China became the 143rd member of the WTO, committing to tariff reductions, market-opening pledges and rules-based dispute settlement. The United States had granted Permanent Normal Trade Relations the year before, locking in the access that accession required.

nodes.title: Obama announces the 'pivot to Asia' from Canberra
nodes.what: In an address to the Australian parliament, President Obama declared that the United States would rebalance its strategic posture toward the Asia-Pacific, including new force deployments in Darwin. The shift was widely read in Beijing as a containment move dressed in engagement language.

cites.l: White House archive - Obama address to Australian parliament

nodes.disputed: The White House described it as a positive reorientation toward a growing region; Chinese state outlets and several US realist commentators described it as the start of an explicit containment strategy.

nodes.title: South China Sea arbitration ruling against Beijing
nodes.what: A tribunal at the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines, finding that China's 'nine-dash line' had no basis in international law and that Beijing had violated Philippine sovereign rights. China rejected the ruling and refused to participate in the proceedings.

cites.l: Permanent Court of Arbitration - South China Sea case

nodes.disputed: Manila and Washington described the ruling as a binding clarification of maritime law; Beijing described the tribunal as illegitimate and the ruling as 'null and void' from the outset.

nodes.title: Trump National Security Strategy names China a 'strategic competitor'
nodes.what: The Trump administration released a National Security Strategy that formally designated China and Russia as revisionist powers and 'strategic competitors' challenging American interests. The document marked the official end of the engagement-era framing in US strategic planning.

cites.l: White House archive - 2017 National Security Strategy

bands.label: Opening and normalization
bands.summary: From Nixon's visit through full diplomatic recognition, MFN battles and the post-Tiananmen recalibration, Washington and Beijing build the engagement architecture that every later frame argues over.

nodes.title: Nixon arrives in Beijing
nodes.what: President Richard Nixon landed in Beijing for a week-long visit and met with Mao Zedong and Premier Zhou Enlai. The trip ended decades of frozen relations between Washington and the People's Republic and produced the Shanghai Communique, in which both sides acknowledged differences over Taiwan while pledging to work toward normalization.

cites.l: US State Department Office of the Historian

nodes.title: Full diplomatic recognition takes effect
nodes.what: The United States formally switched recognition from the Republic of China on Taiwan to the People's Republic of China, and the two governments exchanged ambassadors. Deng Xiaoping visited Washington weeks later, the first PRC leader to do so, and the two sides signed agreements on science, technology and cultural exchange.

cites.l: US State Department Office of the Historian
